page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16 physical cores with 16 vCPUs under a shared CPU allocation model, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance split between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is rated in the bottom 10 percent, and single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3 decompression are weak, placing in the bottom 25 percent. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and PassMark CPU scores all landing in the middle 50 percent. Memory bandwidth tests also show average performance, with read-only small block cached memory reaching 696.35 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 34.59 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation and older Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 architecture, this instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained peak single-core performance. It is suitable for database operations, Redis caching, and static web serving. It is less suitable for intensive LLM inference, where a 7B model drops to a weak 8.11 tokens per second for text generation, or for workloads requiring high-speed local storage.
